# Wiki Fact Placement

A fact has one home: one surface on a page, one owning page type across pages, and one place its build state is recorded. This lookup holds those placement rules.

**See also:** `wiki-authoring-spec` — for the readability rules and the list of every author-facing lookup.

## One home per surface

A page carries the same fact on at most one of its own three surfaces, and the surfaces are not
interchangeable. **Frontmatter** holds the typed, machine-read fact — the engines traverse it, and a
link's edge LABEL in `_derived/cited-by.md` comes from the frontmatter field it was declared in, which
no body link can supply. The **body** holds what frontmatter cannot: prose, an annotation, a link for
which no field exists. An **`index.md`** holds page listings, never a page-level fact — it is
regenerated by reindexing, so anything hand-curated there that a page already owns is lost or
stale by the next rebuild.

Three consequences, which is the whole rule:

- **No body restatement of a typed field.** A section whose content is the value of a frontmatter
  field duplicates it — `heading-restatement` reports this for scalar fields, and the same reasoning
  holds for a link field a template tells an author to copy. A body section may _say something about_
  the feature a page serves; it may not re-list it.
- **A `## Related …` body section is contained by `related:`.** The two are deliberately different
  surfaces — the prose says what a path list cannot, which is why `heading-restatement` exempts list
  fields — but every link the body names must also appear in `related:`, which may carry more. A
  body-only link is still counted in `_derived/cited-by.md`; what it loses is its field label, so
  containment is what keeps every named relation typed.
- **A pointer lives on the page, not in the index.** An external artifact's URL rides in the page's
  own pointer field (`artifacts:` on a design surface or component) or in the `origination: mirror`
  fold; a sub-wiki index carries the page that describes the artifact, not a second copy of its URL.

## Fold pointers

A fact two page types both ask for has one owner and one set of citers, declared in
the fact-ownership lookup's §Fact ownership. Two placement rules govern how a template states its side.

**The instruction goes in the section's own body comment, never in the docblock.** A docblock is read
against the sections its own template declares, so an instruction there naming another type's section
reports as routing content to a section that does not exist. The body comment is also where the author
is already reading when they would otherwise restate the fact.

**A pointer must itself be legal from the shallowest layer its type may occupy.** This is why a
cross-sub-wiki fold rule is stated in this lookup and in the fact-ownership lookup rather than in a sub-wiki
README: a README citation would cross a boundary the layer order forbids wherever a citing type sits
in a sub-wiki that may not cite the owner's. A README keeps what is its own sub-wiki's routing. Where
the layer order forbids the link outright, the fact moves or partitions, as the fact-ownership
lookup's §Fact ownership sets out.

## Realization membership

Whether a page has a build state of its own, and whether a code citation naming it grounds
anything, is decided by one rule. A page is a **realization entry** when it declares one of:

- `realizes:` — the substrate types (`system-component`, `api-contract`, `integration`,
  `ui-component`, `algorithm`), `design-system` and `layout-pattern`.
- `feature:` on a `ui-surface-impl` — the build spec for a feature's surfaces. Its design
  counterpart `ui-surface` carries the same value and is **not** an entry; the pair is
  separated by type, not by which field is present, or one build fact would count twice.

A `test-scenario` is **not** an entry: its `verifies:` links are verification-axis pointers,
and the page carries no build state. A task flow has no entries either; its build state is
derived from the features that list it under `## Task flows`, so a flow reads built when
every listing feature is built, partial when some is built or partial, and a flow no
feature lists has no build state.

A resolved `@realizes` code citation grounds its target as built only when that target is an
entry. A citation naming a **grouping** page — `feature`, `product-module`, `task-flow`,
`app-base` — grounds nothing here, because a grouping's build state is the rollup over the
entries that name it, and marking it built directly would leave that arithmetic with no
denominator. A citation naming a page outside the graph — `architecture`,
`data-model-entity`, `system-entity` — grounds nothing either; both are read by the
code-to-wiki audit instead.

The build state itself is never written on the page. It is recorded off-page, in the
project's dev-status cache, for the reason `wiki-page-content-rules` §Code citations gives: code
cites the wiki and a page never points at code, so a page naming a source path would invert
the direction. A page therefore declares its _membership_ and reads its _state_ elsewhere.

_Authoritative for authors. The engine implements the same rule in the work-entry runtime's
realization grounding; the two are a pair, so change them together._
